A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUBSAMPLE-MFQ research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including the new Appendix K in v4.

before.justification: Appendix B reports original constrained-exploration and Gaussian-squeeze simulations, with reward gaps, computation times, and cumulative rewards in Figure 2.

after.justification: Appendix B and Figure 2 retain the original simulation results on constrained exploration and Gaussian squeeze.

M1.justification: Appendix K adds two heuristic execution procedures, Algorithms 5–6, using weakly or strongly shared randomness. Group-based sampling and majority voting for the global action substantially extend the independent subsampling execution in v3. The original learning algorithm remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same constrained-exploration and Gaussian-squeeze tasks. The added federated-learning example in Appendix J is conceptual, and Appendix K establishes no additional evaluated domain or scenario.

E2.justification: Appendix B and Figure 2 retain the same value-iteration/mean-field benchmarks, including the k = n comparison. The new execution variants are not accompanied by reported baseline comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain unchanged: the 6-by-6 exploration grid, n = 8 exploration agents, n = 8 and 50 Gaussian-squeeze simulations, m = 20 Bellman samples, and 300 execution iterations in Figure 2a. No revised experimental protocol is documented.

E4.justification: The same analyses of subsampling size, reward gap, computation time, and cumulative reward are retained. Appendix K provides heuristic procedures and discussion, without reporting an additional evaluated ablation, robustness test, or case study.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains the same error bars. Neither version explains their construction, and v4 adds no experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All three Figure 2 plot assets are identical across versions, and Appendix B retains the same findings. Appendix K mentions simulations but presents no additional numerical or qualitative performance outcomes.

T1.justification: v4 removes the assertion that total variation is not an f-divergence and generally lacks data processing, previously stated in Section 4 and the remark following Lemma E.8. This corrects the mathematical rationale; the existing convergence bounds and proof derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: subsampled mean-field learning, polynomial dependence on k, a decaying optimality gap of order approximately 1/sqrt(k), and extensions to stochastic rewards, off-policy learning, and continuous spaces.

C2.justification: New Remarks 4.5–4.6 discuss horizon dependence and potentially loose discount-factor dependence; expanded Remark 4.9 explains heterogeneity costs. Appendix K adds limitations concerning sampling overhead and excessive determinism, while Example J.7 illustrates federated-learning applicability.

D1.justification: v4 adds a repository URL described as providing supporting algorithm and experimental code, in Section 2 and Appendix B. The previously documented hardware and experimental parameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations supporting discussion of variance reduction, derandomization, and expander methods, including Sidford et al., Wainwright, Larsen et al., and Reingold. The main mean-field MARL and centralized-training/decentralized-execution positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The original narrative is retained with localized wording edits, additional remarks, a federated-learning example, and Appendix K. Author and acknowledgement text changes. Numerous cross-references now incorrectly call retained lemmas or assumptions 'Theorem,' introducing editorial inconsistencies.

P2.justification: v4 adds two algorithm boxes, reflows the author block, relocates existing algorithm floats, and changes some equation displays and numbering. Figures 1–4 and Table 1 retain their substantive contents.

improvement.justification: v4 improves code-access documentation, removes the incorrect total-variation statement, and clarifies complexity tradeoffs. However, Appendix K claims simulations without presenting outcomes, and Algorithm 6 uses the nonpositive expression n - ceil(n/k)k as a residual action length. With the core results unchanged, these clarity gains and newly introduced reliability problems leave the net quality change unclear.
